spec.title: codkit PROP-012: Output and messages, NFRs, documentation, open decision points

status.comment: standalone schema-2 output, errors, quality and documentation contract

json-envelope.title: 1. The --json envelope

p.JSON-ENVELOPE-RULE: With `--json` every command prints exactly one JSON object to stdout (the human-readable output goes to stderr). The schema of the envelope is versioned by the `codkit.schema` field. The consumers are agents and CI.

errors.title: 2. Human-readable errors and the code registry

p.ERROR-FORMAT: The format: `error CK-E-<KEBAB>: <text with file:line>` plus the next line `hint: <what to do>` (a concrete command where possible).

p.ERROR-REGISTRY: The full registry of the codes is kept in `packages/codkit/src/lib/messages.ts` (the single definition). The codes required by the specifications: `CONFIG`, `NOT-A-REPO`, `NOT-UPSTREAM`, `PIN-UNREACHABLE`, `LFS`, `LOCKED`, `DIRTY-TREE`, `CRLF`, `EOF-NEWLINE`, `ENCODING`, `MARKER-MALFORMED`, `MARKER-NESTED`, `MARKER-UNBALANCED`, `MARKER-UNCLOSED`, `MARKER-DUP-ID`, `MARKER-BAD-ID`, `HUNK-OUTSIDE-MARKER`, `DELETES-UPSTREAM-LINE`, `DELETES-UPSTREAM-FILE`, `NEW-FILE-IN-UPSTREAM-ZONE`, `FORBIDDEN-TARGET`, `MARKER-ARTIFACT-MISMATCH`, `UNTRACKED-INTERVENTION`, `STALE-ARTIFACT`, `OWN-UNCOVERED`, `OWNER-UNKNOWN`, `OVERLAY-SCHEMA`, `OVERLAY-DRIFT`, `RULE-DRIFT`, `ARTIFACT-BROKEN`, `NET-FORBIDDEN`, `LOG-INCOMPLETE`, `BOTH-SIDES-EDITED`, `WORKTREE-REF-SHARED` (the generated branch is one for all the worktrees of the repository; load/cycle refuse to move it while a sibling worktree stands on it - both trees are named, every ref, index and worktree is left untouched; PROP-008 §3 `##GENERATED-REF-WORKTREE-PREFLIGHT`), `TREE-HEAD` (the HEAD of the fork tree is off the generated branch while there are foreign commits on its line, or the history under the generated tip has been rewritten; `load` and `save` refuse with a recipe for getting back - exit 1, nothing touched; PROP-008 §4 `##TREE-COMMITS-ARE-WORK`, decision D8 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE), `SYNC-IN-PROGRESS` (the two-way `codkit sync` did not finish and left a transaction record - the tree and the patch set are half in one state and half in the other; `load`/`save`/`sync` refuse and `status` names the record; PROP-008 §5a `##SYNC-TRANSACTION`, PROP-006 §1 `##SYNC-TRANSACTION-FILE`, decision D20 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE), `INTERNAL` (an uncaught error - a bug, exit 2, the hint is to attach `--verbose`), `DEPS-MISSING` (no runtime dependencies - restore the installed Codkit from the approved supply; a source checkout may run `npm ci`), `TREE-READONLY` (no right to write into the tree or `.git/codkit` - the check `##ID-CHECK-WRITE`), `HEADER-MISSING` (a new patch without a draft header - PROP-007 §8 `##PENDING-HEADER-MECHANISM`), `GUARD-MISSING` (the mandatory guard test is missing, or its id is not declared in the own tests - verify), `FORBIDDEN-SERVICE` (own code overrides a bootstrap service from forbiddenServiceIds - verify), `LICENSE-HEADER` (a file of the package without a carrier of the licence information, or with a wrong carrier - PROP-014 §3), `LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY` (a third-party file breaks the rules of the registry: it is not covered by a `REUSE.toml` annotation, its licence is outside the allowlist, the carrier and the annotation diverge, the notices are stale - PROP-014 §2–3), `LICENSE-PACKAGE` (the package is not consistent: the manifest, `LICENSE`, `LICENSES/`, the symbolic link - PROP-014 §3), `STANDARDS-DRIFT` (the installed copy of the standards package or the copy of the notice differs from the shipped one - `standards load` refuses without writing anything; PROP-014 §5), `RUNTIME-DRIFT` (the installed copy of the runtime library differs from the shipped one - `runtime load` without `--upgrade`, `runtime check`, `verify`; PROP-015 §4), `RUNTIME-PACKAGE` (toolRoot holds not exactly one runtime version directory, or the version literal does not match the name of the directory; PROP-015 §1), `DELIVERED-EDIT` (`save` found an edit of a delivered Codkit file in the tree; PROP-005 §12), `OWN-UNDER-CODKIT` (an own unit whose root is inside `codkit/`; PROP-005 §12), `HOOK-TOO-LARGE` (a patch of type hook exceeds the graft budget; PROP-005 §12), `GEN-EXISTS` (the generator does not overwrite an existing file; PROP-015 §5), `GEN-ID` (a feature identifier not of the required form; PROP-015 §5), `OWN-EXTENSION-MANIFEST` (the `extensions` section of the manifest is invalid, there is no `package.json`, or the name coincides with an upstream extension; PROP-005 §13), `OWN-EXTENSION-DRIFT` (the extension in the tree differs from the delta; PROP-005 §13), `TYPE-UNKNOWN` (the `type` of `codkit.json` is not in the registry of this codkit, or the package the registry names for it is not installed; PROP-016 `##TYPE-UNKNOWN`), `TYPE-CAPABILITY` (a verb needs an ability the declared project type does not have, or `verify` was asked about an artifact of a layer that type does not provide; PROP-016 `##TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`); the warnings `CK-W-*` (at the minimum: `MARK-RO`, `PATCHSET-SIDE-EDIT`, `EMPTY-BLOCK`).

p.USAGE-ERRORS-ARE-CODELESS: CLI usage errors (an unknown command or flag, extra arguments) carry no `CK-E-*` code: `error: …` plus `hint: …` are printed to stderr, exit 2, with no JSON envelope - this is a typo of the operator, not a state of the system. A failure to start git (the binary is not found) is `CK-E-INTERNAL` with the hint «install git ≥ 2.40». (An M0 implementation decision; separate `USAGE`/`GIT-MISSING` codes are deliberately not introduced while no machine consumer needs them.) The borderline code bindings adopted in M0: «the file extension has no marker form» → `FORBIDDEN-TARGET` (symmetrically to a binary target); any violation of the schema or the version of a `.ckpatch`, and a patch file name that cannot be encoded, → `ARTIFACT-BROKEN`; a path with `__` that cannot be encoded into a patch name → `INTERNAL` (there are no such paths at the pin - a protection for the future); a duplicate id between artifacts of any layers → `MARKER-DUP-ID` (reused - no separate «artifact» code for a duplicate is introduced); a violation of «scripts only» on the `package.json` overlay target is a CHECK (`OVERLAY-SCHEMA`, exit 1 in verify/check/apply), not a parse refusal: the document is syntactically valid, it is its content that is inadmissible. The M1 bindings (`ci`): a pin-guard mismatch → `CONFIG` with exit 1 (the stretch of the meaning of the code is deliberate; a separate code is introduced once a machine consumer appears, the M2 cycle skill for instance); `DEPS-MISSING` is reused for the `node_modules` of the TREE in `ci --profile build` (exit 2, with the supply-kit text) - the hint depends on the context (the launcher: «run npm ci»; ci: the cache or mount).

p.LOGS-INVENTORY: The logs: the cycle journal is PROP-009 §3 (md + jsonl, both committed); the daemon logs are `.codkit/build/*.log` (rotation: on `up` the old log is renamed to `.1`, one generation is kept); `--verbose` prints diagnostics to stderr (the git commands with their arguments, the timings of the steps).

docs.title: 4. The documentation shipped with the code

p.M3-OPERATIONAL-DOCS-IMPL: The standalone README, the generated `commands.md`/`conventions.md`/`faq.md`, the CI examples and the air-gapped supply-kit contract are implemented. `docs:check` is built on the live CLI, registries and configs. A documented PowerShell or macOS path does not count as natively proven until it has run on the corresponding runner.

facts.DOC-README: `codkit/README.md` - what this is, the three developer commands (`load`/`status`/`save`), a link to the reference.
facts.DOC-COMMANDS-REF: `docs/codkit/reference/commands.md` - the command reference (generated from the CLI definitions - the single definition of the flags lives in the code).
facts.DOC-CONVENTIONS-REF: `docs/codkit/reference/conventions.md` - the conventions: markers, ids, layers, branches (a rendering of `conventions.json` plus the text of PROP-003…005).
facts.DOC-FAQ: `docs/codkit/reference/faq.md` - the typical refusals (by the code registry of §2) and the traps, retold in plain words.
facts.DOC-CI-EXAMPLES: `docs/codkit/ci-examples/` - the Dockerfile, the Jenkinsfile, the GitHub job (PROP-011 §8) plus the document of the air-gapped supply kit (PROP-011 §7).
facts.DOC-STANDARDS-PAGE: `docs/codkit/protocol/human/13-standards.md` - the delivery of the standards into a product (`standards load` → `vibe install` → `standards check`), the rule of the tail after the manifest block, what to do on `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`.
facts.DOC-RUNTIME-PAGE: `docs/codkit/protocol/human/14-runtime.md` - the Codkit runtime inside a product: `runtime load` → the graft at the composition root → the `code-import-patterns` block per `LAYERS.md` → `gen feature` → the inspector and the simulator; the type bench; what to do on `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` and `CK-E-DELIVERED-EDIT`; what not to do (do not edit `codkit/`).
facts.DOC-TYPES-PAGE: `docs/codkit/protocol/human/15-project-types.md` - the project type of a patch set: what a type is, the two configuration fields (`type`, `typeConfig.ownRoot`), what `codkit types` and the `codkit.type` of `where` print, the refusals `CK-E-TYPE-UNKNOWN`, `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` and the schema-1 `CK-E-CONFIG` with what to do about each, the capability table with the verb that refuses without each one, and the procedure of starting a patch set of a given type. The pages it changes the ladder of - 02, 03, 08, 13, 14 - refer to it instead of repeating it.
facts.DOC-PROTOCOLS-POINTER: The human and the agent protocol are separate slices, FEAT-003/FEAT-004 (only the links are here).

open-forks.title: 5. Open decision points (the work continues on the default)

facts.FORK-TREE-PRECOMMIT-HOOK: **The pre-commit hook in the fork tree is the NORM, rewritten by the owner decision RP-1 of campaign TREE-COMMITS-SAVE (the ruling verbatim: «вместо запрета сделать напоминание»; the original norm of 2026-08-31, «согласен с обеими утверждениями», installed a rejecting hook and is cancelled by this decision).** The hook NEVER rejects a commit: a commit in the tree is work (PROP-008 §4 `##TREE-COMMITS-ARE-WORK`), since phases 2–4 of the campaign it is not lost - the destructive commands refuse over it (`##DRIFT-GUARD-PREDICATE`) and `save` extracts it - so a refusal protected nothing. The hook prints a reminder to stderr: on a `codkit/applied/*` branch, «codkit: this commit is work in the fork tree; it reaches patchset only when you run codkit save or codkit sync»; off it, with the branch in existence (a detached HEAD included), «codkit: HEAD is not on codkit/applied/<tag>; codkit save will refuse until you switch back (git switch codkit/applied/<tag>)» with the concrete `<tag>` of this tree substituted at installation time (`save` will refuse there with `CK-E-TREE-HEAD`, decision D8). `CODKIT_INTERNAL_COMMIT=1` suppresses the reminder (only codkit's own git calls set it; load, however, builds the branch through commit-tree/update-ref, which the hook does not interfere with by construction). `load` installs the script only into the repository's own administrative path - `hooks/pre-commit` under the absolute git directory of the tree (an ordinary tree: `<tree>/.git/hooks/pre-commit`; the rule of the administrative paths is PROP-008 §3 `##TREE-HOOK-STEP`), never following `core.hooksPath` outside the administrative directory of the repository; the hook is restored by every `load` with the current branch name. Exception 1: in a linked worktree the hook is not installed and `load` issues a warning - the hooks are shared by the whole repository, and the reminder would speak in the name of the branch of one tree even in the sibling worktrees that codkit does not manage; the protection there is the refusal of `load`/`save` over foreign commits (the implementation is PROP-008 §3). Exception 2: when a configured `core.hooksPath` (of ANY scope - local/global/system; both are checked, REPAIR-006) leads the git hooks away from the hooks directory of the repository, the administrative copy is installed but git keeps executing the configured hook - `load` warns and `writeTreeHook()` returns false: the reminder is unavailable and unprovable while that configuration stands (honest diagnostics instead of a silent copy that does not work; a refusal to resolve the path - `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, for instance - is also unavailable-with-a-warning and never «active»; the location of the configured hook is not codkit's business). Exception 3: a FOREIGN `hooks/pre-commit` (without the ownership marker `# codkit-hook v1`) is neither overwritten nor chained to: a warning, false, and the bytes are preserved exactly - the same ownership discipline as for the patch-set hooks (REPAIR-006). AN OPEN ARCHITECTURAL POINT (with the owner for consideration): a worktree-scoped hook requires `extensions.worktreeConfig` and management of a per-worktree `core.hooksPath`; it is not authorized in this task. Upstream installs no hooks (the `hooks/` of the effective location is empty apart from LFS) - the place is free. The implementation is a step of `load` (PROP-008 §3), acceptance scenario S20.
facts.RELEASE-REF-NAMING: **The naming scheme of the published release refs.** The `codkit/release/…` namespace and the trailers are defined; the final versioning scheme of the product is not. The default: the branches `codkit/release/<short-sha patchset>+<pin.tag>`, the release tags `patchset-v<semver>+<pin.tag>` (both coordinates in the name). **It requires an owner decision** once a real release process of the product appears.
